citation.title: The Application of the Theory of Moral Blameworthiness in Psychology to the Determination of Punishment for Crimes Arising from Artificial Intelligence Systems
citation.venue: International Journal of Body, Mind and Culture 13(4):235–248

reading.source_scope_note: Conceptual, normative and doctrinal synthesis proposes a chain-of-responsibility assessment of human/institutional culpability. It explicitly reports no fieldwork, interviews, survey, experiment or case-based statistics. Twenty findings are analytical conclusions, not twenty measured psychological effects. No tested AI consciousness, universal legal standard or actual criminal finding is established.
access_limits: Complete supplied article and eight-item bibliography read. Public publisher PDF exactly matches supplied bytes. Primary landing page at https://ijbmc.org/index.php/ijbmc/article/view/1303 and Crossref verify identity, authors and pages. No new duplicate-study credit is assigned.

No supplementary dataset, protocol, code, jurisdiction-specific case analysis or validated allocation/punishment formula is supplied. Data/materials available upon request is not publicly inspected original data. No request was sent and no authors contacted.

NIST primary publication metadata and abstract inspected: Elham Tabassi, 26 January 2023, NIST AI100-1, DOI10.6028/NIST.AI.100-1; the framework is voluntary. The full report was not independently read here. Its malformed AI, N. author entry and 100–101 locator are not independent studies or valid page-level evidence.

EUR-Lex official search metadata identifies Regulation(EU)2024/1689 and Directive(EU)2024/2853; direct document pages returned JavaScript robot-verification screens. Full provisions, exclusions, implementation dates, national transposition and criminal-law standards were not audited. No challenge bypass or current-law conclusion is inferred.

OECD instrument endpoint required JavaScript; the supplied organization/container establishes a corporate legal-instrument reference, not a personal author called Instruments, O.L. Complete instrument text, amendment history and jurisdictional legal force were not independently checked.

Cushman, Malle, Fischer/Ravizza, Matthias, Searle and Sparrow are secondary here; no new full-original reading credit. Other project reviews can hold different philosophical positions. No author-code execution, paid inference, private access, legal adjudication or full-paper Markdown archive.

study.type: Descriptive-analytical conceptual/normative legal-philosophy article; no original human/AI experiment, quantitative synthesis, observed crime or judicial dataset.
study.selection: States relevance, peer review/foundational influence, official-instrument status and recency criteria. It gives no database/search dates, complete query, screening flow, extraction scheme or systematic-review reproducibility protocol. Treat as selected synthesis, not exhaustive psychology/legal evidence.

wrongdoing_categories.accidental_harm: May require correction or compensation without criminal punishment; no automatic exemption or universal remedial rule is established.
wrongdoing_categories.negligence: Failure to meet a reasonable duty of care, assessed using foreseeable risks and practical control/access rather than hindsight alone.
wrongdoing_categories.recklessness: Conscious disregard of a substantial risk, distinguished conceptually from a care failure without established conscious awareness; actual legal elements vary.
wrongdoing_categories.intentional_misuse: Deliberate use of AI for wrongdoing; source gives hypothetical crime examples, not verified incidents or a universal penalty ranking.

study.agency: Distinguishes causal, functional, intentional and moral agency. The claim that current AI lacks consciousness, moral understanding, free will and genuine reasons-responsiveness is an argued philosophical position, not a newly measured result or a resolved empirical test. Functional correction/retraining differs from criminal desert.
study.distribution: Responsibility can be distributed across a lifecycle while remaining differentiated by actual knowledge, duty, authority, opportunity and causal contribution. No single operator or institution is automatically guilty, and a remaining blameless case is possible. A framework cannot guarantee that an actual culpable actor exists in every incident.
study.control: Relevant control must be practical, role-specific and time-sensitive; a supervisory label is insufficient. Foreseeability must be assessed ex ante with known limits and feasible alternatives. Lack of documentation can hinder attribution but is not automatically proof of negligence or intentional concealment.
study.reliance: Source discusses automation bias and expressly allows reasonable reliance to mitigate blame. It also considers ignored warnings/professional verification duties. It supplies no new reliance experiment or universal legal culpability threshold. Keep the broader revised parent definition rather than revert it to unchecked reliance alone.
study.organization: Proposes attention to unsafe incentives, weak audit/data practices, inadequate testing, speed pressure and misleading safety claims. These are candidate organizational fault grounds, not measured prevalence, proof of motive or a validated new independent institutional mechanism.
study.legal_scope: The article itself distinguishes risk-based regulation, civil compensation, administrative sanctions and criminal punishment. It recognizes stricter criminal justification and jurisdictional differences. Legal doctrines require actual elements, defenses, causation, evidence and due process, not merely a generic moral taxonomy.
study.regulatory_sources: EU AI Act and revised Product Liability Directive are discussed repeatedly but have no precise official entries in the eight-item bibliography. NIST2023/OECD2019 citations are not substitutes for those2024 acts. NIST is a voluntary framework; recommendations are not enacted criminal offenses or proof that all listed military/medical uses share one legal classification.
study.reporting: Methods page239 and limitations page246 deny participant/empirical work. Page248 thanks all participants and says voluntary human participation/Helsinki protocol. These declarations are inconsistent with the described design, plausibly template text but cause not established. No hidden sample, fabricated data or misconduct verdict is inferred.
study.limitations_acknowledged: The source explicitly states conceptual rather than empirical scope, current/near-future focus, selected international/European frameworks, jurisdictional variation and need for future research. Preserve those acknowledgments; Original Research front-matter wording does not by itself make a conceptual article invalid.
study.interventions: Specialized investigation bodies, expert panels, audits, documentation and lifecycle duties are proposals. No comparative fairness, victim-protection, prevention or punishment-proportionality benefit is evaluated. They do not install a new authorization layer in this project.

summary: Add Negligence as a care/duty failure distinct from the existing recognized-risk Recklessness concept. Enrich existing responsibility, blame, role, reasons-responsiveness and reliance entries without equating causation, moral fault and criminal liability. Correct malformed institutional-source references and flag participant/ethics declarations inconsistent with the explicitly nonempirical design. Keep different project positions on AI blameworthiness visible.

findings.definition: Failing to exercise the care reasonably required to guard against a foreseeable risk.

evidence.quote: failed to meet a reasonable duty of care

findings.novelty_rationale: A duty-of-care failure need not establish conscious disregard of a known risk, which defines the existing Recklessness record. It is also distinct from rational automation reliance, an accidental bad outcome, generic laziness or mere causal contribution. This is a normative behavioral concept, not a new empirical psychological mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: The conceptual article distinguishes accidental, negligent, reckless and intentional wrongdoing and applies role, knowledge, foreseeable risk, control and prevention criteria across an AI lifecycle. No actual negligence determination or outcome study is reported.
findings.boundary: A harmful outcome alone is insufficient. Specify the legitimate duty, reasonably available evidence, feasible care and relevant role at the time. Moral/civil negligence and criminal negligence differ by jurisdiction and thresholds; an AI process failure does not prove subjective awareness, a guilty mental state or a person’s legal liability.
findings.ai_proposal: For an authorized task, specify required reasonable checks, foreseeable material risks, available evidence and practical time/capability limits. Audit whether an assistant performed the necessary care before acting. Separate failure of a feasible check from justified reliance, unavoidable accident and proceeding despite an explicitly known unjustified risk; preserve actual human/institutional ownership.
findings.origin: Moral responsibility / duty-of-care and criminal-law analysis
findings.ai_evidence_status: Conceptual distinction in a fully read normative article; no AI experiment, observed negligence episode or jurisdiction-specific legal test is validated.

findings.definition: Proceeding despite a recognized substantial risk of harm without giving that risk the consideration it warrants.
findings.novelty_rationale: Preserve existing concepts of fault, reliance and distributed responsibility. The current theoretical synthesis does not supply a new observed blame effect or make moral, legal and causal responsibility interchangeable.
findings.evidence_scope: The source distinguishes recognized substantial-risk disregard from negligent care failures, accidents and intentional misuse in a proposed culpability framework.
findings.boundary: A known risk can be justified given necessity, proportionality, alternatives and safeguards. Source categories are not a universal mutually exclusive criminal code or automatic penalty scale. Do not infer awareness or intent from an adverse output.

findings.definition: Assigning fault or responsibility to an agent for a negative event or outcome.
findings.novelty_rationale: Preserve existing concepts of fault, reliance and distributed responsibility. The current theoretical synthesis does not supply a new observed blame effect or make moral, legal and causal responsibility interchangeable.
findings.evidence_scope: The article applies a structured appraisal of causal contribution, knowledge, duty, control and preventability to differentiated human/institutional roles.
findings.boundary: No observed blame judgment, validated predictor weighting, actual crime or deserved sanction is measured. Causal involvement and public blame do not determine legal liability; legitimate rights, evidence and remedies remain separate.

findings.definition: Difficulty assigning individual moral responsibility when many actors contribute to a collective outcome.

evidence.quote: across the entire AI life cycle

findings.novelty_rationale: Preserve existing concepts of fault, reliance and distributed responsibility. The current theoretical synthesis does not supply a new observed blame effect or make moral, legal and causal responsibility interchangeable.
findings.evidence_scope: The proposed chain allocates inquiry across design, data, training, deployment, oversight and use, resisting an exclusive focus on the final user.
findings.boundary: Distributed contribution does not prove nobody is responsible, everybody is culpable or one corporation must be punished. Evidence for duty, control, knowledge and causation is actor-specific; a purely blameless harm remains possible.

findings.definition: Having duties and being evaluated for their fulfillment because of a specific role.

evidence.quote: meaningful control over the relevant risk

findings.novelty_rationale: Preserve existing concepts of fault, reliance and distributed responsibility. The current theoretical synthesis does not supply a new observed blame effect or make moral, legal and causal responsibility interchangeable.
findings.evidence_scope: The paper differentiates what designers, trainers, deployers, users and regulators can know, control or prevent, and links prospective duties to actual roles.
findings.boundary: A role label does not itself establish feasible control, a legitimate duty or culpability. Do not scapegoat a worker with insufficient authority, information or resources; institutional and individual duties can coexist.

findings.definition: A capacity to recognize morally relevant considerations and adjust decisions or actions appropriately in response to them.
findings.novelty_rationale: Preserve existing concepts of fault, reliance and distributed responsibility. The current theoretical synthesis does not supply a new observed blame effect or make moral, legal and causal responsibility interchangeable.
findings.evidence_scope: The authors treat genuine responsiveness to moral reasons as a proposed condition for full blameworthiness and distinguish it from functional goal-directed output selection.
findings.boundary: This is a philosophical commitment rather than a demonstrated capacity test. Behavioral responsiveness, understanding, free will, sentience and criminal desert differ. Retain opposing arguments elsewhere in the project rather than resolve them by assertion.

findings.definition: Attributing to an entity the capacity to understand moral considerations, make ethical judgments and bear responsibility for its choices.

evidence.quote: not be treated as morally blameworthy agents

findings.novelty_rationale: Preserve existing concepts of fault, reliance and distributed responsibility. The current theoretical synthesis does not supply a new observed blame effect or make moral, legal and causal responsibility interchangeable.
findings.evidence_scope: The article argues against granting present systems full human-like moral/criminal subjecthood while preserving human and institutional accountability.
findings.boundary: A defended normative position is not an empirical agency-attribution effect or evidence that all responsibility theories agree. No model internal state or actual legal-personhood determination is tested.

findings.definition: Unduly relying on automated cues, or their absence, despite practically accessible evidence that warrants checking or overriding them.
findings.novelty_rationale: Preserve existing concepts of fault, reliance and distributed responsibility. The current theoretical synthesis does not supply a new observed blame effect or make moral, legal and causal responsibility interchangeable.
findings.evidence_scope: The discussion distinguishes reasonable reliance on a presented-safe system from ignored warnings or omitted professional scrutiny. It is conceptual application to culpability, not new reliance data.
findings.boundary: Justified reliance is not bias merely because a later outcome was wrong. Retain the revised parent’s feasible-access and evidential-warrant boundary, including attended counterevidence; no automatic criminal liability or universal verification duty follows.

findings.definition: A pattern in which a human operator bears disproportionate blame or responsibility for failure in a complex automated system despite having limited control over its actions.
findings.novelty_rationale: Preserve existing concepts of fault, reliance and distributed responsibility. The current theoretical synthesis does not supply a new observed blame effect or make moral, legal and causal responsibility interchangeable.
findings.evidence_scope: The argument warns against treating a reasonably relying end user like a corporation knowingly deploying an unsafe system.
findings.boundary: Context only: no measured disproportionate blame or actual institutional blame-shifting episode is established. Role comparison can be warranted; a low-level operator is not always blameless or always solely responsible.

findings.definition: Taking an appropriate role in acknowledging and redressing harm connected to one’s agency despite the absence of blameworthiness for causing it.
findings.novelty_rationale: Preserve existing concepts of fault, reliance and distributed responsibility. The current theoretical synthesis does not supply a new observed blame effect or make moral, legal and causal responsibility interchangeable.
findings.evidence_scope: The source allows accidental harm to call for correction or compensation without criminal punishment.
findings.boundary: Context only: this is compatible with, but not an independent validation of, the prior relational account of blameless responsibility. Compensation is not an admission of fault, and a generic possibility is not a universal damages entitlement.

findings.definition: A condition in which necessary work lacks clear, accepted and adequately supported ownership among the actors involved.
findings.novelty_rationale: Preserve existing concepts of fault, reliance and distributed responsibility. The current theoretical synthesis does not supply a new observed blame effect or make moral, legal and causal responsibility interchangeable.
findings.evidence_scope: The paper addresses difficulty locating a blameworthy subject in a distributed learning-system incident.
findings.boundary: Context only: a backward-looking culpability gap differs from unowned operational monitoring/repair work. Neither proves the other, and the current source does not audit real task ownership or maintenance practice.

source_corrections.finding: NIST primary page identifies Elham Tabassi,26January2023,Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework(AI RMF1.0),report NIST AI100-1,DOI10.6028/NIST.AI.100-1. Replace the malformed personal-author parse and do not treat report identifier100-1 as a100–101 passage range. Only metadata/abstract were inspected,not the whole report.

The cited item is an OECD institutional Council recommendation/legal instrument,not a person called Instruments,O.L. Preserve OECD-LEGAL-0449 and the actual corporate/institutional identity. The direct endpoint is JavaScript-only here; no full-text or amendment-history audit is credited.

source_corrections.location: EU AI Act and revised Product Liability Directive citations
source_corrections.finding: The discussed instruments are Regulation(EU)2024/1689 and Directive(EU)2024/2853. Neither has a precise entry in the supplied eight-item bibliography; surrounding NIST2023/OECD2019 citations cannot identify those statutes. Official EUR-Lex search metadata verifies the identities,not full current-law scope or national applicability.

source_corrections.location: Page248 participant/ethics declarations versus pages239/246 methods/limits
source_corrections.finding: The article expressly denies human/empirical work yet thanks participants and states voluntary participation under a Helsinki protocol. The reporting statements are inconsistent. Template residue is a possibility,not an established cause; do not infer an undisclosed study or fabricated dataset.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: No jurisdiction-specific statutory elements, judicial cases, defenses or sentencing comparison is analyzed sufficiently for a present legal determination. Standards of negligence, mens rea, strict liability and corporate criminal liability vary. The source itself calls for comparative work.

The categorical lack-of-consciousness/understanding/reasons claim is not experimentally tested. Other philosophical sources in this corpus defend different limited accountability or attributability positions. Preserve the disagreement and distinguish current legal responsibility from unresolved mental-capacity questions.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.location: Chain model efficacy and unavoidable blame
unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: The source argues the chain avoids impunity/over-punishment,but no case validation or comparative outcome test establishes this. Actual harm can be blameless; identifying a chain is not proof that someone violated a duty.

Poor documentation can be evidence relevant to a feasible duty; opacity is not automatically intentional concealment,negligence or guilt. Knowledge,access,control,causation and ex ante feasibility must be shown separately.

Eight selected references and stated selection principles do not constitute a reproducible systematic review or complete regulatory audit. NIST/OECD do not independently supply a new empirical automation-bias result or determine a criminal threshold.

Publisher classifies Theoretical Study(ies),PDF says Original Research,while method is explicitly conceptual. April issue/online date and July file generation can coexist; exact revision history is not established. No fraud,retraction or priority inference follows.

Specialized investigators,expert judicial panels,auditing and documentation are recommendations without measured comparative benefit. They do not impose a new approval body or action gate on this authorized project work.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Findings means a hidden human dataset was analyzed
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The methods and limitations explicitly deny empirical work. Findings are analytical conclusions; inconsistent participant boilerplate does not establish a hidden sample.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: The article equates civil,regulatory and criminal responsibility
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: It repeatedly distinguishes them and states that risk classification/civil compensation do not alone justify criminal punishment. Its exact legal coverage is limited,but the conceptual separation is explicit.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Every reliance error is culpable bias in this account
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The source expressly allows reasonable reliance to mitigate blame and distinguishes ignored warnings/professional duties. Do not omit that qualification.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: No current AI punishment implies no human accountability
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The central argument preserves differentiated human/institutional accountability. That does not prove an actual guilty actor exists in every blameless incident.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: July PDF metadata falsifies April publication
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Regenerated files can postdate initial publication. Public publisher bytes match the supplied file; revision history is unresolved rather than proven false.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Causal contribution,functional assessment,attributability,answerability and blameworthiness differ. The present article rejects full machine criminal desert; the catalogue must not collapse that into one universal meaning of responsibility.
Preserve competing arguments about how AI could be blameworthy. The current categorical rejection is a philosophical stance,not a new empirical refutation of that earlier position.
Faultless harm can still call for acknowledgment and repair. A chain of involvement does not guarantee culpability,and a repair duty is not automatically punishment or confession.

Reliance must be assessed against practical evidence access and ex ante warrant. The earlier weak/strong distinction remains broader than the current unchecked-output gloss; no parent definition rollback is warranted.

Role responsibility can exist without full moral accountability. Specify actual duties and capabilities and retain human institutional ownership rather than infer personhood or scapegoat the operator.

deferred.term: Design recklessness/deployment negligence as independent new mechanisms
deferred.reason: Role-specific applications of Recklessness and Negligence,not separately validated mechanisms. Preserve lifecycle/actor distinctions in study metadata rather than duplicate rows.

deferred.term: Organizational culpability and chain model as newly validated behavior effects
deferred.reason: Normative allocation level and proposed assessment framework. Existing many-hands,role and blame records cover the relationships; no unique measured mechanism or proven intervention is supplied.

deferred.term: Mens rea,strict liability and punishment as new psychology failures
deferred.reason: Legal elements,liability regimes and responses,not equivalent observable AI mental behaviors. Keep the source’s taxonomy and jurisdiction limits rather than infer subjective guilt or a universal legal rule.

deferred.term: Foreseeability/control/preventability as five independent psychological effects
deferred.reason: Assessment dimensions requiring role/time/evidence-specific judgment. Preserve as analytical criteria without inflating them into independent experimentally validated mechanisms.

deferred.term: Moral blameworthiness as an exact synonym of causal responsibility
deferred.reason: The source expressly distinguishes deserved censure from causal contribution. Existing blame/agency/responsibility records preserve the distinction.

limitations: One normative behavioral record added and seven existing records receive bounded conceptual evidence; three receive non-counted context. Catalogue becomes800 across eleven categories,not800 independent psychological mechanisms. Stable IDs,unnumbered rows,seven evaluation criteria and six ethical principles retained. No automatic harm links,forced citation quota,invented annual totals,new participant data,legal adjudication or full-paper Markdown archive.
